statement: You are given an array values that is k-sorted: every element is at most k positions away from where it belongs in sorted order. Return the array sorted in ascending order.

Because of that guarantee, the smallest remaining element is always among the next k + 1 unplaced elements. So keep a min-heap of size k + 1: fill it with the first k + 1 elements, then repeatedly pop the minimum into the next output slot and push the next unread element. This takes O(n log k) time instead of O(n log n).

examples.explanation: No element is more than 3 places from its sorted position; 6 and 2, for example, each move exactly 3. A heap of 4 elements is enough to emit the values in order.
Every element is within 2 places of its sorted position, so a heap of 3 elements always holds the next value to output.
A fully reversed array of 4 elements is 3-sorted, since 4 and 1 each move 3 places. Here the heap holds the whole array at once.
